nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 preparation and surface treatment
nodes.procedure: Ni(OH)2 was prepared and then treated with a diluted 57Fe3+ solution to place Fe ions on the surface of Ni(OH)2 (for the synthetic procedure, see Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: In the next step, Ni(OH)2 was prepared and then treated with a diluted 57Fe3+ solution to place Fe ions on the surface of Ni(OH)2 (for the synthetic procedure, see Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Precipitation synthesis
nodes.procedure: By mixing Ni and 57Fe ions with KOH, NiFe (hydr)oxide is formed, where a higher concentration of Fe ions is present in the bulk compared to the surface.
nodes.source_text: By mixing Ni and 57Fe ions with KOH, NiFe (hydr)oxide is formed...

nodes.name: Oxidation synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiO(OH) was synthesized via the reaction of Ni2+ ions and ClO- according to a previously reported method.

nodes.description: In situ ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy - bulk NiFe (hydr)oxide
nodes.source_text: Initially, Fe⁴⁺ (3.5%) was detected at 1.45 V, which increased to 8.7, 27.1, 47.1, 55.4, and 55.6% at 1.50, 1.55, 1.63, and 1.68 V, respectively... Analogous to the initiation of Fe⁴⁺ formation, the onset of the OER manifests at 1.45 V
The results of ⁵⁷Fe Mossbauer spectroscopy revealed that only Fe³⁺ was present at the RDS; even at 1.68 V, no Fe⁴⁺ was detected for the compound

During chronoamperometry, Fe³⁺ oxidation occurs, but no increase in OER current density is observed... At 1.68 V, after 1 min, 24 h, and 96 h, the proportions of Fe⁴⁺ decreased from 55.56% (at 1.68 V) to 54.14%, 53.97%, and 52.02%, respectively.

stability.value: unstable until Ni³⁺ reduced to Ni²⁺

nodes.source_text: Fresh NiO(OH) was unstable and underwent the OER when dispersed in a KOH solution... The OER persisted until a few Ni³⁺ ions were reduced to Ni²⁺... For two months, a subtle transition in the color of NiO(OH) from black to gray was observed

nodes.name: Ni²⁺ hydroxide treated with ⁵⁷Fe ions

nodes.characterization_summary: CV of pure Ni wire before/after adding Fe salt (1 ppm) shows four OER regions: i) NiO/NiO(OH) ≈100 mV, ii) Fe-related 200-300 mV, iii) Fe/Ni mixed ≈300-450 mV, iv) Ni-related >1270 mV with Fe leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Before and after Fe salt was added (final concentration: 1 ppm), the cyclic voltammogram profile (CV) at a potential range of 1.25-3.25 V for a pure Ni wire ... Four distinct regions were found for the OER according to the experimental results (Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ visible spectroscopy of FeOₓ shows no peak below 1.45 V, peak at 475 nm at 1.45 V, additional peaks at 560 and 660 nm at higher potentials; OER onset at 1.60 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For FeOₓ, in situ visible spectroscopy showed no peak below 1.45 V, but at 1.45 V, a small peak was recorded at 475 nm. At higher potentials, along with this peak, other peaks were observed at 560 and 660 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Fe K-edge XAS of NiFe (hydr)oxide under OER and OCP shows Fe³⁺ state (peaks similar to FeO(OH), Fe₂O₃); XANES/EXAFS show Fe-O coordination number changes; ex situ shows decreased Fe-O/Fe-Fe/Ni bond lengths.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe oxidation states in NiFe (hydr)oxide under OER potential and open circuit potential (OCP) conditions were investigated, revealing that the positions of the peaks were similar to those of FeO(OH) and Fe₂O₃, which denoted the Fe³⁺ state (Note 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer of NiFe (hydr)oxide shows two Fe sites (Fe_A, Fe_B) before OER; Fe⁴⁺ increases from 3.5% at 1.45 V to 55.6% at 1.68 V and remains >50% after 96 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Initially, Fe⁴⁺ (3.5%) was detected at 1.45 V, which increased to 8.7, 27.1, 47.1, 55.4, and 55.6% at 1.50, 1.55, 1.63, and 1.68 V, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer of Ni²⁺ hydroxide treated with ⁵⁷Fe³⁺ shows only Fe³⁺ at RDS (1.68 V); no Fe⁴⁺ detected on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of ⁵⁷Fe Mossbauer spectroscopy revealed that only Fe³⁺ was present at the RDS; even at 1.68 V, no Fe⁴⁺ was detected for the compound.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ SERS of Ni₃FeOₓ shows peak at 1165±2 cm⁻¹ related to Fe-based materials; NiO(OH) shows peaks at 475, 560 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni₃FeOₓ during the OER showed a peak at 1165±2 cm⁻¹ related to Fe-based materials or other intermediates in KOH (1.0 M).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows few Fe ions leached into solution during OER of NiFe (hydr)oxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, the ICP-MS inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis revealed that few Fe ions leached into the solution.
